title: Reconnaissance Marine (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
6.     MOS 0321, Reconnaissance Marine (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. The Reconnaissance Marine is a Marine skilled in multi-
domain reconnaissance & surveillance. In addition to basic rifleman skills,
Reconnaissance Marines possess enhanced physical and psychological attributes
required to gain access to the operational environment and are required to
maintain advanced capabilities in combat swimming, small boat operations,
highly-refined scouting and long range patrolling, close combat skills,
demolitions, forward observer procedures for supporting arms, ITG operations
for heliborne, airborne, and waterborne forces; long-range communications,
multi-domain collections, threat weapons and equipment identification. All
Reconnaissance Marines receive advanced training in survival escape
resistance evasion (SERE), low level static line (LLSL) parachuting, military
freefall parachuting, and combatant diving. They are also trained as a
subject matter expert in advanced communications, special weapons, joint
terminal attack control, helicopter rope insertion/extraction techniques,
assault climbing, intelligence collection, mountain warfare, methods of
entry, sniper operations, advanced combat life support, close quarter
tactics, and may serve as jumpmasters and dive supervisors depending on their
billet in the reconnaissance unit. Reconnaissance Marines contribute to the
multi-domain collection of intelligence at the tactical, operational, and
strategic echelons of command. They are highly capable of conducting low
visibility missions in environments ranging from cooperation to conflict.
Supporting the fleet Marine Force, fleet, or joint task force, Reconnaissance
Marines provide timely intelligence to the supported commander to shape and
influence the operational environment. The varying types of missions a
Reconnaissance Marine conducts are multi-domain reconnaissance and
surveillance, battle space shaping, and other special reconnaissance
missions.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Must possess a CL score of 105 or GT score of 105 or higher.
This prerequisite is non-waiverable.

         (3) Security requirement: must have minimum interim secret security
clearance based on national agency check, law enforcement and credit check
(NACLC).

        (4) Marines must possess a water survival-intermediate (WS-I), water
survival qualification to enter the reconnaissance physical assessment
program (RTAP).

        (5) Must possess a water survival-advanced (WS-A), water survival
qualification to enter the Basic Reconnaissance Course (BRC) (M10AHK2).

        (6) Must obtain a passing score in all following land and aquatic
events during the reconnaissance physical assessment program (RTAP):

                (a) Max set pullups–min 8/target reps 15+ 2:00 minute rest.

                (b) Max set crunches–min 75/target reps 85+ 2:00 minute rest.




                                          3-26                         Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



                (c) Max set pushups–min 42/target reps 60+ 10:00 minute rest.

                (d) 3 mile run min 22:30/target 19:30 10:00 minute rest.

                (e) Obstacle course x2–min 8:00.

                (f) 500-meter swim 15 min (side or breaststroke, continuous
swim).

                (g) 25-meter underwater swim.

                (h) Rifle retrieval.

                (i) 25-meter rifle tow.

        (7) Marines must attain passing scores in all elements of the
Reconnaissance Physical Assessment Test and Reconnaissance Aquatic Competency
Test during separate training evolutions and will be required to attain
passing scores to graduate the Basic Reconnaissance Course.

        (8) Must be medically qualified to perform jump and combatant dive
qualifications in accordance with inter-service requirements established in
(ai), NAVMED P-117 and reference (at), standards of medical fitness. Lateral
moving enlisted Marines and officers must have completed naval special
warfare/special operations (NSW/SO) physical prior to reporting to BRC. Entry
level enlisted Marines and officers must complete the NSW/SO physical prior
to reporting to BRC. This includes a report of medical history (DD form 2807-
1) and a report of medical examination (DD form 2808). The completed NSW/SO
physical must be reviewed and countersigned by an Undersea Medical Officer
(UMO). Marines assigned 0321 PMOS who become medically unqualified will have
a medical waiver request submitted by a UMO or may be directed to lateral
move or be reassigned based on the commanding officer, MMEA and HQMC
recommendations.

            (9) Lateral-move additional prerequisites:

                (a) No derogatory page 11 entries within the last 12 months.

            (b) No NJPs within the last 12 months and with no more than one
NJP during the current contract.

                (c) No courts martial convictions.

                (d) Must be a volunteer.

        (10) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xi) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

        (11) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) All entry-level marines must successfully complete the Marine
Combat Training Course (M10M922 or M03M924).




                                           3-27                      Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) Complete the Reconnaissance Training Assessment Program (RTAP)
(M100Z22).

            (3) Complete the Basic Reconnaissance Course (M10AHK2).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer
to reference (ca), Reconnaissance Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Special Forces 55-3018.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Rifleman, 0311.

            (2) Reconnaissance Marine, Sniper Qualified, 0322.

            (3) Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute Qualified, 0323.

            (4) Reconnaissance Marine, Combatant Diver Qualified, 0324.

            (5) Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute and Combatant Diver Qualified,
0326.

            (6) Combat Rubber Reconnaissance Craft Coxswain, 8020.
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
